comparison: Strong agreement on core finding of spatial convergence with temporal divergence (C8-C10, C37-C43). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with robust statistical support including Bayesian analysis. Peer review explicitly affirms this as the central validated finding, noting improved confidence from simulations.

Perfect agreement on HRF convolution control analysis (C46-C48). Both evaluations support that this analysis successfully rules out the alternative explanation that temporal divergence results from different signal speeds. Peer reviewer specifically mentions simulations improving confidence.

Strong agreement on replication findings in scalp EEG-fMRI dataset (C50-C53, C87). Both evaluations treat the replication as successfully confirming main results across different populations and recording modalities. Peer review describes methods as 'solid' and data as 'convincing.'

Strong agreement on study hypothesis and rationale (C3, C32-C34). Both evaluations support the multiplex hypothesis as well-motivated and empirically validated. Peer review describes approach as 'innovative' and confirms the study successfully determined scenario II as most likely.

Strong agreement on dataset quality and methodological approach (C96-C103). Both evaluations affirm the concurrent multimodal recordings as appropriate and the sample sizes as reasonable. Peer review explicitly praises the 'novel approach' and 'robust statistics.'

Agreement on connection-level convergence findings (C49). Both evaluations treat this as successfully contextualizing the novel connectome-level findings within prior literature, showing coexistence of connection-level convergence with connectome-level divergence.

Agreement on reconciliation with prior literature (C72-C73). Both evaluations support the distinction between connection-level and connectome-level analysis as a novel contribution. Peer review notes detailed interpretation placing results in context of recent advances.

Agreement on multi-frequency independence findings (C44-C45, C74-C75, C77). OpenEval emphasizes clustering analysis with null model comparison. Peer review explicitly highlights that different frequencies don't overlap significantly, supporting independent operation of multiple connectivity states.

Partial overlap on clustering and state analysis (C57, C59). Both evaluations support the clustering findings. Peer review extends to multiplex conceptualization (C60, C78, C91) which OpenEval addresses separately as more speculative functional interpretation.

Agreement on small effect sizes and their interpretation (C67-C69, C70). OpenEval explicitly praises transparency in reporting small effects. Peer review implicitly accepts this through acknowledgment of 'moderate to weak' spatial convergence as meaningful, though doesn't explicitly discuss effect sizes.

Agreement on limitations and mitigation strategies (C86-C87). Both evaluations accept that scalp EEG replication adequately addresses spatial sampling limitations of intracranial recordings. OpenEval provides more detailed discussion of multiple limitations (C81-C90).

Divergence in evaluation certainty on functional interpretation (C55-C56, C60, C91, C93-C94). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting functional claims about 'maximizing information flow' are speculative. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 accepting multiplex interpretation and editor affirming functional implications about concurrent processing.

Divergence in evaluation certainty on functional claims (C93-C94 overlap). OpenEval rates functional interpretation as UNCERTAIN/speculative. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with editor explicitly stating work addresses how brain carries out multiple functions concurrently, and reviewers not challenging functional interpretation.

Divergence in evaluation certainty on neurophysiological mechanism (C61-C63). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting interpretation is plausible but speculative since fiber properties weren't directly measured. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED within broader acceptance of detailed interpretation, though doesn't specifically address mechanism claims.

Divergence in evaluation certainty on main conclusions (C11-C12). OpenEval supports 'functionally distinct trajectories' but notes 'enables concurrent connectivity' is speculative. Peer review fully supports both aspects, with editor affirming the work addresses concurrent multi-timescale processing.

Divergence in evaluation certainty on multiplex conceptualization (C78-C79, C92, C95). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting telecommunications analogy is metaphorical and bandwidth claims speculative. Peer review rates multiplex framework as SUPPORTED, treating it as logical extension of temporal divergence findings.

OpenEval specifically evaluates background literature claims (C35-C36) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate characterization of prior work and identification of knowledge gap. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation of these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological choices (C105-C109) including amplitude/phase coupling, HRF delay, correlation type, and clustering approach as SUPPORTED with clear rationale. Peer review discusses methods generally as 'solid' but doesn't separately evaluate these specific methodological decisions.

OpenEval evaluates foundational neuroscience principles (C1-C2, C13-C16) as SUPPORTED, noting they establish well-established concepts motivating the study. Peer review doesn't separately evaluate these background principles.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive background on connectome dynamics and methodological differences (C17-C31) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review doesn't separately evaluate this extensive background section.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization of prior work (C71, C76) as SUPPORTED, distinguishing current connectome-level focus from prior analyses. Peer review mentions this contextualization within broader discussion (R2, R12) but doesn't separately evaluate these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates study design and terminology definitions (C5-C7) as SUPPORTED, noting clear definitions of spatial/temporal convergence. Peer review discusses study design within overall methodology evaluation (R9) but doesn't separately evaluate these definitional claims.
